newsitem.title: USA: Andersen Worldwide names acting CEO.
newsitem.headline: Andersen Worldwide names acting CEO.

text.p: Andersen Worldwide, parent of accounting firm Arthur Andersen, said Monday it named W. Robert Grafton acting chief executive to replace CEO Lawrence Weinbach when his term ends on Aug. 31.
Andersen, which also owns Andersen Consulting, said it has deferred naming a permanent chief executive.
Grafton will remain Andersen's chairman of the board of partners when he becomes acting CEO, a company spokesman said.
Andersen said it will convene a "high-level group" to address organisational issues before it names a permanent managing partner and chief executive.
The group will develop specific proposals for addressing organisational issues by spring 1998, the New York-based company said in a statement.

On Friday, the Wall Street Journal reported that the latest nominee to head Andersen failed to secure enough partner votes to take the post, the second time in less than two months that the board's choice to succeed Weinbach was rejected.
In its statement, Andersen said its partners confirmed at its recent global meeting its preference to keep the organisation together by making "appropriate internal adjustments."
Andersen Worldwide has more than 100,000 employees in over 380 offices in 79 countries. Andersen Consulting and Arthur Andersen had combined revenues of $9.5 billion in the year ended Aug. 31, 1996.
